10297.title: Visiting Professor of Finance
10297.bio:
Hongjun Yan’s research focuses on asset pricing in the presence of frictions and behavioral finance. His studies have been published in the Quarterly Journal of Economics, Review of Economic Studies, American Economic Review: Insights, Review of Financial Studies, Journal of Financial Economics, and Journal of Monetary Economics, among other journals. 

In addition to teaching at Booth, Yan is the Richard H. Driehaus Chair in Behavioral Finance at DePaul University. Before joining DePaul, he taught at the Yale School of Management from 2005 to 2015, and at Rutgers University from 2015 to 2016. He has a PhD in finance from London Business School. 

Yan is the winner of various teaching, research, and referee service awards: Outstanding Research Paper of Year Award, Richard H. Driehaus College of Business, 2026, Selected Project, Fintech Chair at Paris-Dauphine University – PSL, 2025, Constantine "Gus" Economos Distinguished Teaching Award, 2025, Researcher of the Year, Richard H. Driehaus College of Business, 2024, Behavioral Finance Best Paper Award at the 2023 CFRC, Best Paper Award at the 2020 GSU-RFS FinTech Conference, The 2013 Management Science Meritorious Service Award, Winner of NASDAQ OMX Award for the Best Paper on Asset Pricing at WFA, 2011.

10301.name: Leonardo  D'Amico
10301.title: Assistant Professor of Economics and Finance and Liew Family Junior Faculty Fellow
10301.bio:
Leonardo D’Amico joined Booth following his work as a Postdoctoral Research Associate at the Louis A. Simpson Center and at the Department of Economics at Princeton University.  His research areas include finance and macroeconomics, with a focus on spatial economics, real estate, and banking.

D’Amico earned a PhD in Economics from Harvard University. Additionally, he holds an M. Sc. and a B. Sc. in Economic and Social Sciences, both from Bocconi University. In addition to his research activities, in 2021 and 2022 D’Amico worked as a junior economist in the staff of the Prime Minister of Italy.

10302.name: Galina  Kalcheva
10302.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Finance
10302.bio:
Galina Kalcheva is a Portfolio Manager at Aon Investments, responsible for Aon's Private Credit, Real Estate and Infrastructure Fund-of-Funds. Previously, Galina managed the firm's Fund-of-Hedge-Funds and oversaw more than 20 client pension plan and endowment portfolios. Before joining Aon, she was a member of the Municipal Bond Team and a strategist in the Portfolio Management Group of a $90 billion insurance asset manager.

Galina received an MBA from the University of Chicago, and a BS in Finance from the University of South Carolina. Galina is currently pursuing a PhD in Finance from École des Hautes Études Commerciales du Nord (EDHEC).

Additionally, she is a CFA charterholder, and completed the Certificate in Quantitative Finance, a financial engineering program by Fitch Learning.

10303.name: Jason  Sussman
10303.title: Adjunct Associate Professor of Entrepreneurship
10303.bio:
Jason Sussman is the Founder and CEO of 2065 Capital and a Managing Director and Investment Committee Member at The Pritzker Organization, the merchant bank for Tom Pritzker Family business interests. His current and past board positions include Wellspring Family Office, Ferian Re, Steward Partners, Portfolio Group, GreyCastle Holdings and Financeit. He also serves on the advisory councils of the Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering at University of Chicago, the Booth Family Office Initiative, UChicago Hillel, and Invest for Kids.

Previously, he was a vice president in structured finance at Barclays Capital, where he held a proprietary investments role. He started his career as a tax associate at Davis, Polk and Wardwell.

Sussman created and is teaching the course "Structuring Investments and Investing in Structure" at Booth in the 2026 Winter Quarter.   In addition, Sussman has served as a Lecturer in Law at the University of Chicago Law School since 2014.  At the Law School, he created and teaches the course, “Structuring Financial Instruments,” an eight week seminar.

Sussman is a CFA charterholder. He received his BA (summa cum laude, Phi Beta Kappa) and his JD (with high honors) from Columbia University.

10305.name: Gary  Silberg
10305.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Strategy
10305.bio:
Gary Silberg is former Global Head of Automotive and Partner at KPMG, and one of the world’s foremost voices on the future of mobility, artificial intelligence, and transportation innovation. His insights have been featured in Forbes, The Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg, and leading global summits.

For over 25 years, Silberg has been at the forefront of advising top automotive and technology firms — including Ford (as Global Lead Partner), NVIDIA, Rivian, Jaguar, Toyota, and Volvo — on strategy, innovation, and disruption. He has also led the UChicago Booth x KPMG M&A and Economic Forum for the past 23 years, hosting speakers such as Tim Ingrassia (Co-Chairman, M&A at Goldman Sachs), David Axelrod (Former Senior Advisor to President Obama), and Professor Eugene Fama (Nobel Laureate, UChicago) for a total of 11 Nobel Prize winners throughout the years.

In his course, Silberg will bring students face-to-face with global C-suite leaders to explore how industries are being redefined by emerging technologies.

Silberg holds an MBA from Booth and earned a BS in accounting from the University of Missouri-Columbia.

10315.name: Sangeeta  Prasad
10315.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Healthcare Management
10315.bio:
Sangeeta Prasad is a Bio-Pharma professional and Growth Strategist with more than 20 years of experience in the public and private sectors. She brings C-suite expertise, global leadership and a record of consistently exceeding revenue goals with career milestones across developed and emerging markets, including the U.S. and Emerging Markets. 

Sangeeta completed her MBA in 1999 from the Full-time program at the University of Chicago’s Booth School of Business.  She also has an MA in Economics from the Delhi School of Economics. Over the course of her career, she has risen to senior leadership roles, including Senior Vice President of Sales, Marketing, and Business Development in the biotech-pharmaceutical industry. 

Sangeeta specializes in assessing market potential, identifying revenue streams, and developing collaborative models that drive growth and profitability. She has led revenue growth, product strategy, commercial development, branding, and business model innovation for Fortune 500s such as Abbott (now AbbVie) and Sun Pharma, as well as small start-ups that achieved successful acquisitions. Her track record includes planning and executing multimillion-dollar product launches, creating blueprints to launch business units and building high-performing teams and coalitions with stakeholders from the ground up. 

In addition to her professional career, Sangeeta serves on multiple advisory and non-profit boards, where she applies her strategic and execution skills to advance organizational impact. She enjoys cooking, traveling and hanging out with family.

10332.name: Ben  Chabot
10332.title: Adjunct Associate Professor of Finance
10332.bio: Professor Chabot's research focuses on banking, financial markets and the role of institutions on asset prices and financial stability. From 2010-2024, Professor Chabot was an Economist and Senior Policy Advisor at the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago where he advised on financial stability and FOMC deliberations and led a systemwide team of economists and data scientists responsible for producing Dodd-Frank Stress Test results. While at the Fed, Professor Chabot taught undergraduate and Ph.D. Classes at Northwestern University where he served as an Adjunct Associate Professor of Economics. Prior to joining the Fed, Professor Chabot was a Visiting Assistant Professor and Senior Lecturer in both the Economics and History Departments at Yale (2008-2010) and an Assistant Professor of Economics at the University of Michigan (2000-2008). Prior to receiving his Ph.D. in Economics, Professor Chabot was an instructor in Northwestern University's McCormick School of Engineering (1999).

10344.name: Brian  Wolfe
10344.title: Adjunct Associate Professor of Entrepreneurship
10344.bio:
Brian Wolfe is Managing Partner at Funded Ventures, a private investment firm, and is a retired partner at Kirkland & Ellis LLP. In addition to his teaching at Booth, Wolfe also teaches courses on private equity and entrepreneurship at the Northwestern Pritzker School of Law, Washington University in St. Louis and the University of North Carolina, and previously co-led a SaaS “buy and build” with sale to private equity.

Wolfe is on the board and audit committee of Chicago Public Media, the boards of Intersect Illinois, Breakthrough T1D (f/k/a JDRF) Illinois, the Greater Chicago Legal Clinic and the Skandalaris Center at Washington University in St. Louis, and is a member of the Illinois Courts Commission and the Economic Club of Chicago.

10371.name: Carlos  Ganoza
10371.title: Adjunct Associate of Applied Artificial Intelligence
10371.bio:
Carlos Ganoza is an entrepreneur, senior product executive, and economist who has been working with AI since 2014, applying it to solve complex problems across different domains. He co-founded and scaled a machine learning company from a slide deck to a multinational operation, and later joined Wonolo—the leading staffing marketplace—through an acquisition, where he now serves as VP of Product, leading the product organization and AI initiatives. He has deep experience building AI-driven products in SaaS and marketplace models and across B2B and B2C. 

Carlos is an Endeavor mentor, coaching founders from around the world on building technology products, leveraging AI, and achieving product–market fit. He also mentors entrepreneurs working on AI through the University of Chicago's Polsky Center. Recognized as one of Latin America’s Top 100 Innovators by Bloomberg, Carlos has received multiple awards for his work in developing high-impact AI products.

Carlos holds an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business, where he specialized in economics. His career has spanned the public, private, and entrepreneurial sectors: he has served as Chief of Staff at the Peruvian Ministry of Finance, led Peru’s top business media company as CEO, and built and scaled AI products with meaningful social impact. 
He has also co-authored two books on the Peruvian economy. 
Carlos is originally from Peru and has been based in Los Angeles since 2021, where he continues to work at the intersection of technology, economics, and innovation. His passion lies in leveraging innovative ideas to build solutions that address important societal challenges.

10407.name: Thomas  Elnick
10407.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Entrepreneurship
10407.bio: Thomas Elnick is a Partner at Bancroft Capital Partners (BCP), a private investment company focused on building incredible products and businesses with exceptional people. BCP manages solely the Partners’ money and has a patient and long-term investment horizon. Prior to BCP, he was the co-founder and co-CEO of Tegus, a leading research platform serving more than 30,000 public and private market institutional investors, investment bankers, consultants, and corporations. In 2024, Tegus was acquired by AlphaSense for $930m. Elnick received his BA in Economics from Brown University. He lives with his wife and two children in Chicago.

10422.name: Samantha  Coleman
10422.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Leadership
10422.bio:
Bridging psychology, leadership, and storytelling to help leaders align who they are with how they lead—under real pressure and in real time.

Samantha Coleman, PhD, is Senior Associate Director of Leadership Development and Adjunct Faculty at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business. A leadership educator, executive coach, and former therapist, Dr. Coleman draws on her clinical background, social entrepreneurship, and cross-sector experience to design high-impact learning environments that integrate rigor, reflection, and real-world application.

Her work focuses on developing leaders who are both competent and congruent. Grounded in the science of psychological capital—hope, efficacy, resilience, and optimism—her facilitation emphasizes authenticity, empathy, and deep listening as strategic leadership capabilities.          Dr. Coleman has coached and consulted with leaders at every organizational level—from emerging professionals to C-suite executives—across regulated, creative, and operationally complex industries, including healthcare, financial services, social impact, entertainment, automotive, and retail. Her experience includes partnerships with leaders and teams within Fortune 100 and Fortune 500 companies, where she applies a listening-driven, context-responsive approach to leadership development.

Known for creating psychologically safe, feedback-rich learning environments, Dr. Coleman blends behavioral science with experiential methods that emphasize application over abstraction. She also serves as a co-facilitator in Booth’s Interpersonal Dynamics course, bringing a relational, listening-centered approach to some of the school’s most impactful leadership development experiences. Her teaching and facilitation challenge participants to interrogate default leadership scripts, navigate the tension between internal authenticity and external expectations, and translate self-insight into effective communication and action in complex, high-stakes environments.

Beyond Booth, Dr. Coleman is the founder of Do You But Better, a leadership and learning company focused on empathy, authenticity, and resilience, and a co-founder of Black to the Beginning, a storytelling platform amplifying the Black adoption experience. Together, her academic, entrepreneurial, and narrative work reflect an interdisciplinary commitment to helping individuals and systems lead with clarity, intention, and purpose.

10426.name: Bob  Casey
10426.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Entrepreneurship
10426.bio: Bob Casey is the Founder & CEO of Santa Barbara Management (SBM), a fractional family office, and a Partner at Partners Fund Capital, a growth equity firm that invests solely on behalf of its partners. Previously, he was the President and CFO of Tegus, a leading research platform for institutional investors acquired by AlphaSense in 2024 for $930 million. Earlier in his career, he served as a Partner at the Investment Group of Santa Barbara, CEO of MindFlash, VP of Platform at Clover Technologies, and Founder and CEO of YouRenew. Bob holds a BA in Economics from Yale and an MBA from Harvard Business School. He lives in Chicago with his wife and three children.

10449.name: Anshuman  Taneja
10449.title: Adjunct Associate Professor of Marketing
10449.bio:
Anshuman Taneja is the Executive Vice President and Chief Digital & Technology Officer at GNC, where he leads the company’s global digital, product management, data, and technology functions in support of growth, modernization, and customer experience transformation. 

Previously, Taneja served as Chief Product Officer at Gap Inc., overseeing product management and digital platforms across a portfolio of iconic global brands. His career spans senior leadership roles in digital leadership, product management, and technology at organizations including Ahold Delhaize, Abercrombie & Fitch, and Walgreens, where he has led large-scale transformations. 

Across multiple organizations, Taneja has built and scaled product management functions from the ground up, establishing product-led operating models, scaling digital and data capabilities, and aligning technology strategy and execution with commercial outcomes. He has worked extensively at the intersection of strategy, commercial ownership, product, and technology in complex, consumer-facing businesses. 

Taneja holds an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business and has completed executive leadership programs at Harvard Business School. In addition to his operating roles, he serves as an advisor to emerging technology companies and frequently engages with boards and executive teams on digital transformation and innovation.

10456.name: Simcha  Barkai
10456.title: Visiting Assistant Professor of Finance
10456.bio:
Simcha Barkai is visiting from Boston College where he is an Assistant Professor of Finance.  He also serves as a Junior Fellow at the George J. Stigler Center for the Study of the Economy and the State at Booth.  His work in academia extends to the London Business School where he was an Assistant Professor of Finance prior to his time at Boston College.

Barkia studies competition between firms in the U.S. and implications for macroeconomic and asset pricing. His work on the decline in the labor share of income has been covered by The New York Times, Wall Street Journal, The Economist, The Financial Times, Bloomberg, Forbes, Harvard Business Review, The Washington Post, The New Republic, and The Nation.

Barkai holds a PhD in Financial Economics from the University of Chicago.  Additionally, he earned MSc and Bsc degrees in mathematics from Hebrew University.

10457.name: Andrew  Stier
10457.title: Assistant Professor of Behavioral Science and John E. Jeuck Faculty Fellow
10457.bio:
Why does it feel different to live in a large city versus a small one? Scholars across disciplines point to cognitive overload, inequality, and density — but there is little empirical psychological evidence for these claims. Understanding how physical and social environments influence how we interact with each other, how we make decisions, and whether we find happiness and meaning is critical if we hope to design organizations, neighborhoods, and societies that facilitate better lives. Andrew Stier's research works towards these goals by integrating methods from computational cognitive neuroscience, social psychology, and complex systems to understand the interactive feedback between individual minds and environmental context. 

Specific research threads include: (1) measuring the cognitive and behavioral signatures of urban environments; (2) understanding the feedback loops between individual minds and collective behavior; (3) mathematical modeling of how environmental constraints shape cultural affordances. Stier's long-term research goal is to reintegrate explicit models of complex environments into psychological science — an open challenge since Lewin popularized the idea that behavior is a function of interdependent person and environmental factors. Stier's research aims to lead to a relationship between psychology and the social engineering of organizations, cities, and societies similar to the relationship between physics and the engineering of skyscrapers, airplanes, and bridges. 

Stier’s research has been published in impactful journals, including, PNAS, Nature Communications, npj Complexity, and Network Neuroscience. His research has also been featured in the media, including the Times of London and Bloomberg.  He is currently a research fellow at the Sante Fe Institute.

Before joining Booth, Stier was an Omidyar and Emerging Political Economies postdoctoral fellow at the Santa Fe Institute and completed a PhD in Integrative Neuroscience in the psychology department at the University of Chicago.

10462.name: Ravi  Mehta
10462.title: Adjunct Associate Professor of Finance
10462.bio:
Ravi Mehta is a special situations investor with over 18 years of experience investing in opportunistic credit globally. 

Over the course of his career, he has invested across the capital structure and liquidity spectrum.  His experience spans tradeable stressed and distressed debt, structured capital transactions, DIP financings, equity backstops, trade claims, sovereign credit investments, and post-reorganization equities.  Ravi has served on numerous ad hoc creditor groups and boards of restructured companies. 

Ravi teaches a course at Booth on distressed debt investing, where students analyze real-world restructurings to understand how sophisticated investors evaluate complex capital structures and navigate the restructuring process.  He has previously taught a course on distressed debt investing at the University of Chicago Law School. 

He holds an MBA from Harvard Business School and a BA in Economics, magna cum laude, from Harvard College.

10470.name: Agata  Farina
10470.title: Assistant Professor of Accounting and MV Advisors Faculty Fellow
10470.bio:
Agata Farina’s research is in information economics and draws on tools from experimental economics, behavioral economics, and microeconomic theory. She studies how information is strategically produced, disclosed, and interpreted, with a particular focus on how incentives and behavioral biases shape beliefs and decisions. Her work combines formal economic modeling with laboratory experiments.

Prior to joining Booth, she was a Postdoctoral Research Associate in the Department of Economics at Princeton University. Farina holds a PhD in Economics from New York University Stern School of Business, and an MSc and a BSc in Economic and Social Sciences from Bocconi University.

11474.name: Charles  Downing
11474.title: Assistant Professor of Accounting and IBM Faculty Fellow
11474.bio:
Chuck Downing’s research interest is in the economics of technological change. He is particularly interested in the economic consequences of generative AI in driving changes in the accounting labor market, information processing, and the production of accounting information.

Downing earned a PhD in Accounting and holds an MS in Management Research, both from MIT Sloan.  Additionally, he earned a BS in Accounting (with honors) from The Ohio State University.

11479.name: Benjamin  Feigenberg
11479.title: Visiting Professor of Economics
11479.bio:
Ben Feigenberg is visiting from the University of Illinois Chicago, where he is a Professor of Economics. His research focuses on the economics of crime and education, using experimental and quasi-experimental methods. As a researcher, he works to support innovative policy-making at the local and state level. His ongoing projects study the impacts of restorative justice practices in public schools; the effects of rehabilitative programming in state prisons; and racial and socioeconomic disparities in the U.S. criminal justice system.

In addition to his faculty position at the University of Illinois Chicago, Feigenberg is a Faculty Research Associate at the National Bureau of Economic Research.

Feigenberg received a PhD in economics from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and holds a BA with honors in economics and Latin American studies from Brown University.

11481.name: Richard  Thakor
11481.title: Visiting Associate Professor of Finance
11481.bio:
Richard T. Thakor is a Visiting Associate Professor of Finance at the University of Chicago’s Booth School of Business. He is on leave from the University of Minnesota’s Carlson School of Management, where he is an Associate Professor of Finance and also serves as the school's undergraduate Honors Program Coordinator. Thakor is a Research Affiliate at the MIT Laboratory for Financial Engineering (LFE), and is a Research Affiliate at the WFA Center for Finance and Accounting Research (WFA-CFAR) at Washington University in St. Louis. He joined the Finance department at the University of Minnesota in 2016 after earning his PhD in Financial Economics from MIT. He also holds an M.S. in Management Research from MIT, an MSc in Finance and Economics from the London School of Economics (LSE), and a B.A. (summa cum laude) in Economics and Psychology from Washington University in St. Louis. Prior to earning his PhD, he worked in investment management as a Derivatives Trading Analyst.

Thakor does research in empirical and theoretical corporate finance, in the broad areas of R&D and innovation, financial institutions, and the effects of financial frictions on firm investments. An area of focus of his research agenda is healthcare finance, exploring how financial markets shape the drug development process as well as the delivery of healthcare to patients. He has published numerous research papers in leading journals in Finance, Economics, Management, and Healthcare, including the American Economic Review, Journal of Financial Economics, The Review of Financial Studies, Management Science, Nature Biotechnology, and Health Affairs.

Thakor is a co-author (with Zvi Bodie and Robert C. Merton) of Principles of Finance, a textbook for introductory and follow-on Finance courses written for undergraduate and MBA audiences. He has taught courses at the undergraduate, MBA, Masters in Finance, PhD, and executive levels. He has won multiple teaching awards, including Minnesota Carlson Undergraduate Instructor of the Year and being named by Poets & Quants as one of the top 50 undergraduate business professors of 2024.

11484.name: Antonio  Coppola
11484.title: Assistant Professor of Finance and Fama Faculty Fellow
11484.bio:
Antonio Coppola joined Booth from the Stanford Graduate School of Business, where he was an Assistant Professor of Finance. His research uses large-scale micro data and applied AI methods to study questions in international macroeconomics and finance and in macro-finance. He has worked on topics including machine learning methods in financial regulation, global capital flows, tax havens, financial stability, reserve currencies, and real-time economic measurement with unstructured data.

Coppola is also a Faculty Research Fellow at the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER), a Research Affiliate at the Centre for Economic Policy Research (CEPR), and a Faculty Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research (SIEPR). He serves as an Associate Editor at the Journal of the European Economic Association (JEEA).

Coppola received a PhD in Economics from Harvard University.  He also earned an A.B. Summa Cum Laude in Applied Mathematics from Harvard University.

11551.name: Jason  Jackson
11551.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Entrepreneurship
11551.bio:
Jason Jackson is a Partner at Futaleufu Partners and Co-Founder of the Black Search Network. He previously acquired and exited Unified Dental Partners through a traditional search fund — a journey recognized as a case study in Stanford Graduate School of Business' Entrepreneurship Through Acquisition course.

Drawing on his operating experience, Jackson speaks at business schools and serves as a trusted resource for search fund entrepreneurs navigating the transition to the CEO role.

11555.name: Michael  Schwert
11555.bio:
Michael Schwert is a Principal and Chief Investment Officer at AQR Arbitrage, an affiliate of AQR Capital Management specializing in arbitrage and corporate event strategies. He leads the arbitrage portfolio management team and helps shape research and strategy development. Schwert rejoined AQR Arbitrage in 2023 after an earlier tenure with the firm as an Analyst (2009-2011).

Prior to rejoining AQR Arbitrage, Schwert was an Assistant Professor of Finance at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania (2018-2022) and The Ohio State University Fisher College of Business (2016-2018). His academic research has been published in leading finance journals and recognized with awards including the Q-Group Jack Treynor Prize and the Jacobs Levy Center Research Paper Prize for “CLO Performance,” and the Marshall Blume Prize in Financial Research for “Does Borrowing from Banks Cost More than Borrowing from the Market?” 

Schwert received his Ph.D. in Finance from the Stanford Graduate School of Business in 2017 and B.S. in Mathematics and Economics (with High Distinction in Economics) from Duke University in 2009.

11567.name: Evan  Moore
11567.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Entrepreneurship
11567.bio:
Evan Moore is an investor and entrepreneur who cofounded DoorDash and was previously a Partner at Khosla Ventures. 

He began his career in the music industry, where he worked at Universal Music Group and helped develop and launch Vevo. He later attended Stanford’s Graduate School of Business, where he cofounded DoorDash as a student. Evan then joined the founding team of Opendoor, leading product and helping build several of the company’s early teams. In 2018, he joined Khosla Ventures as a Partner, where he led financings across seed, venture, and growth stages and worked closely with roughly 30 founding teams. 

Today, Evan invests independently, backing about 15 startups per year, typically at the earliest stages. He also invests in emerging venture funds and serves on the board of Teamshares (NASDAQ: TMS).

11609.name: Ramon  Melgarejo
11609.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Marketing
11609.bio:
Ramon Melgarejo currently serves as President of Consumer Intelligence and eCommerce at NielsenIQ.  Previously he had global responsibility for the Innovation (BASES) and Advanced Analytics divisions. He has dedicated his career to redefining how businesses understand and engage with their customers. Melgarejo’s journey in the industry is marked by innovation and an unwavering commitment to providing dynamic insights that impact consumers.

Over a career that spans 23 years across NielsenIQ and Affinnova, Melgarejo has worked and overseen teams across sales, customer success, operations, and product leadership teams. Under his leadership, clients receive value-driven solutions that enhance consumers’ lives and foster long-term success.

Throughout his career, Melgarejo has been instrumental in driving innovation in consumer insights, recognizing the vital role of dynamic information in today’s fast-paced marketplace. His deep understanding of consumer behavior, thoughts, and actions, combined with an agile and predictive approach, has transformed how businesses operate.
